correctness.rationale: An exact disjoint-record count computes the full conditional success-by-arrival-position masses, independently reproduced by exhaustive enumeration for all cutoffs through eight candidates. A strictly increasing tail likelihood ratio reduces full-CDF first-order stochastic order to one last-position comparison and exactly the displayed harmonic expression. Uniform harmonic asymptotics with the published optimal threshold rounding and joint equidistribution yield a valid density-area argument; boundary and exceptional bands have zero natural density. The finite standard-library checker passes, but does not establish any infinite-limit theorem.

originality.rationale: The genuinely new statement is an exact stochastic-order dichotomy for success-conditioned arrival-time distributions and the explicit positive natural density of incommensurable horizon-dependent reversals. The motivating paper proves total success probabilities, threshold corrections, and rectangular rounding frequencies, not this CDF comparison or nonrectangular sign area. The older two-choice secretary formulas account for total winning events, not their conditioned time ordering. Search found no claim that directly states or implies the density law; however general historical priority cannot be guaranteed.
residual_risks: Historical general secretary-success-time ordering results may imply parts of the exact conditional law; no universal uniqueness claim is made.
Full text of the 2023 combinatorial query-model paper was unavailable; its distinct mechanism reduces, but does not eliminate, priority risk.
The central threshold-rounding theorem and Weyl independence are explicitly imported from the cited 2026 source rather than reproved.

value.rationale: Selecting a globally best candidate earlier is a natural performance measure of sequential decisions even when both strategies succeed. The theorem classifies all finite cutoff pairs by a sharp harmonic inequality and reveals that seemingly benign integer-rounding effects reverse a qualitative stochastic order on a strictly positive, explicitly computable fraction of large horizons. It goes beyond success-probability optimization and ordinary approximations to rounded thresholds.
